chapter: Opening and photographs of New Orleans bands
title: Photo of celebrities at the Famous Door with George Girard
summary: Coquille names Lou Salino, George Girard, William Bendix and Harold Cooper in a photo taken at the Famous Door, with praise for Girard.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well, back in the 30s and 40s and early 50s, you had quite a few celebrities that always came into the famous store every night. And this was shot, I don't know who shot this particular photograph. But anyway, it's a photograph taken of Lou Saino, trombone player, who later went with the Louie Primer group, traveled all around the country with Louie Primer for about 12 years before forming his own group and returning. Well, he did a little road work with his own group, Lou Saino, and then he is currently working in New Orleans at the Maison Bourbon every night with his own group. He's one of the three bands at Maison Bourbon, on Bourbon and St. Peter. He has the night shift from about 9 to 1, something like that. Next to Lou Saino is the late George Girard. I should say the late fabulous George Girard, because he had so much personality. He was a very excellent player and had so much front line personality. He completely had the audience in the palm of his hand every night. That was a great loss when George passed away at the age of 27. And next to George Girard is the late William Bendix, the movie idol who gave us so much happiness in his TV shows. And next to William Bendix is the late Harold Cooper, who recently passed away, I think within the past year. And everyone knows Harold Cooper. He played for many years and traveled all over extensively with the late Dukes of Dixieland, the original Dukes of Dixieland. And next to Harold Cooper is Marcel Bob Coquille, who was playing string bass here with the late George Girard at the famous door.
